How shelter dog day trips work

More and more shelters let people take adoptable dogs out for a few hours or a night. The dogs get a break from the kennel, and you help them get seen by future families.

What is a day out?

A day out (also called a field trip, daycation or doggy day out) is a short outing with a shelter dog: a walk, a hike, a coffee run or an afternoon on your couch. Many shelters also offer sleepovers or weekend staycations.

How to sign up

Find a program on ShelterDayOut, then follow the link to the shelter's own page. Most ask you to fill out a short form, show an ID, and sign an agreement. Some take walk-ins; others need a reservation. The shelter picks a dog that fits your plans.

Who can go?

Programs marked Open to the public (189 so far) welcome anyone who meets the shelter's rules, usually 18 or older. Volunteers only programs are for the shelter's trained volunteers, and many shelters make it easy to become one.

Tips for a great outing

Bring water and a bowl, keep the dog on leash, skip dog parks, and take lots of photos. Share them and tag the shelter: good photos are one of the best ways to help a dog find a home. If you fall in love, ask about adopting.

What about cats?

Cats usually prefer to stay put, so cat programs look different: staycations at home, lounge visits and kitten fostering. See cat programs.

ShelterDayOut is a free directory. We don't run outings or handle bookings; each shelter sets its own rules. Listings are checked monthly, but details change, so confirm with the shelter before you go.

Ready to adopt? ShelterAdoption, our sister site, lists every shelter near you plus upcoming adoption events.
